about: Stages and timing for the reachable-audience playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: reach
stages.do: Measure how much of the base can be reached by channel, the consent gap and the monthly opt-ins against opt-outs, as the baseline; add the gaps as findings and ask the user which channel to grow.

stages.name: on-site
stages.do: Check whether a capture form (newsletter or phone sign-up weblayer) already runs, whether it was ever tested, and what else shows on the same pages.

skip_when.reason: the reach stage found no consent gap worth closing.

stages.name: build
stages.do: Write the capture form's weblayer code (or a challenger to the existing form), recording consent the way the project does, for the user to paste into an inactive weblayer in the Engagement UI.

skip_when.reason: the reach stage found no consent gap worth closing.

stages.name: qa
stages.do: QA the inactive weblayer until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the build stage's skill (engagement-weblayer-builder) and the user pastes it. Then wait for the user to launch it as an A/B test in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the launch as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: the reach stage found no consent gap worth closing.

stages.name: read-out
stages.do: Read the capture test's result on sign-ups. Don't stop early on a good-looking day.

skip_when.reason: the reach stage found no consent gap worth closing.
the qa stage was skipped, so no launch was recorded.

stages.name: recheck
stages.do: Run the audit again with the baseline's base and categories: did reach on the chosen channel and the monthly opt-ins grow since the launch?

skip_when.reason: the reach stage found no consent gap worth closing.

notes.min_test_days: Days after the qa stage finishes (the day the user launched the form) before the read-out is due. engagement-experiment-readout calls a winner only after at least 14 days in whole weeks; use the planned end date when it's later.
notes.recheck_after_days: Days after the launch before the recheck is due. contactability-audit reads consent changes by calendar month, so about 60 days gives at least one full month after the launch to set against the baseline's months.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then. no_winner and no_clear_change are the ways out when the wait never gives an answer.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped; skips don't cascade, so each stage lists every earlier outcome that ends the run). Every stage skill is read-only: engagement-weblayer-builder returns code the user pastes, and the user creates the weblayer, sets the split and launches it in the Engagement UI, so the playbook is read-only and the launch is recorded as a change with source engagement-ui. The test is the weblayer's own A/B split (the new form against a Control group, or a challenger against the existing form); engagement-experiment-readout reads weblayer splits from banner events when asked. The on-site stage decides between a new form and a challenger to an existing one. A capture form grows reach only among visitors; re-permission for people with an address but no consent is a message, built outside this run (engagement-segment-builder, then a campaign), and a scenario A/B test can be set up with engagement-ab-test-setup for it; it isn't a stage.
